A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CodeBrain’s two-stage MRI-imputation work. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable throughout. v1 includes Supplementary Material A–D; the supplied v2 ends after its references, allowing retained, revised and omitted material to be compared.

before.justification: v1 reports original IXI and BraTS 2023 imputation experiments, ablations and supplementary quantitative and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 reports original imputation results, quantization and component ablations, and downstream brain-tumor segmentation experiments.

M1.justification: The main procedure now extracts common features from concatenated, masked available modalities instead of a randomly selected single modality. However, this all-source variant was already evaluated in v1 Appendix C/Table B. v2 adopts it as the standard procedure while retaining the two-stage architecture, scalar quantization and grading loss.

E1.justification: IXI, BraTS 2023 and their MRI modality coverage remain unchanged. v2 adds downstream brain-tumor segmentation of completed BraTS scans, materially extending evaluation beyond reconstruction and imputation to a distinct clinical task absent from v1, including its supplement.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains MMSYN, MMGAN, MMT and M2DN as imputation comparators. The new segmentation comparison in v2 Table 4 evaluates MMT and M2DN alongside newly introduced zero-imputation and full-modality reference conditions.

E3.justification: Reported training changes from 150 to 250 epochs per stage, and IXI code dimension increases from 7 to 9; dataset splits remain unchanged. VQ comparisons use revised configurations, including 256-dimensional vectors and two codebook sizes. The new segmentation protocol evaluates a U-Net under four three-to-one imputation settings using 2D/3D Dice and an additional prediction-reference evaluation.

E4.justification: v2 adds continuous-versus-discrete latent-code ablations and reworks the VQ comparison. Figure 5 jointly tests common features and grading loss across dimensions 5, 7 and 9, replacing the earlier dimension sweep and separate component table. Segmentation tests downstream utility and 3D consistency. v1’s BraTS source-specific and single-versus-all-source analyses in Appendix C are omitted.

E5.justification: Both versions specify random seed 1234 and report point estimates without repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. v2’s paired 2D/3D Dice values represent different metrics, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces CodeBrain’s default IXI aggregate PSNR/SSIM of 29.01 dB/92.09% with 29.43 dB/93.01%, and BraTS values of 25.02 dB/89.09% with 25.16 dB/90.09%. These accompany changed model/training settings, not a same-setting comparison. Baseline scores remain unchanged, while CodeBrain becomes best on BraTS SSIM. New ablation and segmentation results are added; the detailed BraTS imputation breakdown in v1 Table C is omitted.

T1.justification: Equation 1 corrects the bounding transformation from Z_a = floor(L/2) tanh(Z_a) to Z_a = floor(L/2) tanh(F_a), removing the self-reference. The remaining quantization and loss mathematics is substantially retained; neither version contains theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain unified MRI imputation through compact codes, two-stage training and a grading loss. v2 adds an explicit introduction-level contribution that CodeBrain-imputed modalities facilitate BraTS tumor segmentation. Calling the codes modality- and instance-specific largely clarifies properties already described in v1.

C2.justification: v1 explains inferior BraTS SSIM through absent structural supervision; v2 interprets revised scores as evidence of invariant anatomical representation and adds claims about near-real segmentation and 3D consistency. It also argues that continuous latent spaces complicate transformation. The limitations discussion replaces texture-detail deficiencies with hallucination concerns, especially for T1Gd, and removes the dataset-bias caveat.

D1.justification: Resource disclosures change from 94.85 GMACs/96.44 million parameters to 157.82 GMACs/134.56 million parameters, with IXI training time changing from 36 to 84 hours. v1’s 42-hour BraTS runtime is omitted. v2 specifies VQ codebook configurations; hardware, software, data-access links and the prospective code-release promise remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to the BraTS 2023 meningioma challenge, Physics of MRI: A Primer, and Online Clustered Codebook. It removes works supporting earlier disentanglement, anatomical-guidance and fairness discussions. The broad positioning against pixel-to-pixel imputation and explicit-codebook approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial introduction passages are rewritten around a divide-and-conquer explanation. Dataset and implementation subsections are merged, and the separate Discussions section is integrated into Ablation Studies and Discussions. The title, author list and contribution footnote change, and the standalone supplement is absent from v2.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is completely redrawn into separate training-stage panels. Figures 3–4 reorganize scans and error maps; the dimension plots become grouped ablation bars, and code visualizations expand to all nine channels. Table 1 incorporates reconstruction results, Table 4 becomes a segmentation comparison, and the supplementary figures and tables are omitted.

improvement.justification: The continuous-versus-discrete controls and downstream segmentation evaluation provide useful validation missing from v1, while the revised pipeline diagram improves clarity. These gains are tempered by loss of detailed BraTS supplementary evidence and overbroad segmentation interpretations: for missing T1Gd, CodeBrain’s 3D Dice is 43.35%, below M2DN’s 48.62%. Higher imputation scores also accompany changed model and training settings. Overall, the added diagnostic evidence supports a limited quality improvement.
